label: Bible Study
prompt: Favour is _____, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
verse: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
note: The last word on the virtuous woman — charm fades, beauty passes, reverence lasts.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: _____ art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the LORD, the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency! and thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee; and thou shalt tread upon their high places.
verse: Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the LORD, the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency! and thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee; and thou shalt tread upon their high places.
note: Moses's final blessing ends with a cheer: Happy art thou, O Israel — a people saved by the LORD.

label: Sunday School
prompt: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on _____, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
verse: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
note: One reluctant sermon, and all Nineveh put on sackcloth — from the greatest of them to the least.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Is it _____ to you, all ye that pass by? behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow, which is done unto me, wherewith the LORD hath afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
verse: Is it nothing to you, all ye that pass by? behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow, which is done unto me, wherewith the LORD hath afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
note: Jerusalem in ruins calls out to people walking past: is there any sorrow like mine?

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For I am _____, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
verse: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
note: The start of Paul's great list — death, life, angels, powers — that climaxes in verse 39: nothing can separate us.
